This surah is Madani.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} The Exalted says, addressing His Prophet [Muhammad] (ﷺ) and the believers: {O Prophet, when you divorce women}; that is, when you intend to divorce them, {then}: seek for their divorce the lawful manner, and do not hasten to divorce as soon as its cause arises, without observing the command of Allah. Rather, {divorce them for their 'iddah}; that is, for the sake of their 'iddah (waiting period): the husband should divorce her while she is in a state of purity (tuhr) in which he has not had intercourse with her. This is the divorce in which the 'iddah is clear and manifest. This is unlike divorcing her while she is menstruating, for then that menstrual period in which the divorce occurred is not counted, and the 'iddah is lengthened because of that. Likewise, if he divorces her in a purity in which he has had intercourse with her, then her pregnancy cannot be ruled out, so it is not clear by which 'iddah she is to observe the waiting period. Allah commanded the counting of the 'iddah, that is, the reckoning of it by menstrual cycles if she menstruates, or by months if she does not menstruate and is not pregnant. In counting it there is the fulfilment of the right of Allah, the right of the divorcing husband, the right of whoever will marry her afterwards, and her right to maintenance and the like. When her 'iddah is accurately reckoned, her condition is known with insight, and what follows for her of rights and what is due to her from them becomes known. This command to count the 'iddah is directed to the husband and to the wife if she is legally responsible; otherwise, it is directed to her guardian. And His saying {and fear Allah, your Lord}; that is, in all your affairs, and fear Him regarding the rights of the divorced wives.

{Do not turn them out of their houses}: during the period of the 'iddah, but she must remain in the house in which her husband divorced her. {Nor should they leave}; that is, it is not permissible for them to leave it. As for the prohibition against turning her out, it is because the dwelling is obligatory upon the husband for the wife, so that she may complete her 'iddah in it, and it is one of his rights. As for the prohibition against her leaving, it is because her leaving involves wasting the husband's right and failing to protect it. This prohibition against leaving the houses and against expelling from them continues until the 'iddah is complete. {Unless they commit a clear immorality}; that is, a clearly ugly act that necessitates her expulsion, such that not expelling her would bring harm upon the household, such as harm through ugly words and deeds. In this case it is permissible for them to expel her, because she is the one who caused her own expulsion, and housing her is a consolation to her and kindness to her; it is she who brought harm upon herself. This applies to the revocable divorcee (raj'iyyah). As for the irrevocably divorced woman (ba'in), she has no obligatory residence, because residence follows maintenance, and maintenance is due to the revocable divorcee but not to the irrevocably divorced one.

{These are the limits of Allah}; that is, which He set for His servants, legislated for them, and commanded them to adhere to and stand by. {And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah}: by not standing by them, but exceeding them or falling short of them, {he has certainly wronged himself}; that is, he has diminished his own right and lost his share of following the limits of Allah, which are the good in this world and the Hereafter. {You know not; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter}; that is, Allah legislated the 'iddah and limited divorce by it for great wisdoms. Among them: perhaps Allah will place mercy and affection in the heart of the divorcing husband, so he will take back the woman he divorced and resume marital life with her, and he can do so during the period of the 'iddah; or perhaps he divorced her for a reason from her side, which will disappear during the 'iddah period, so he takes her back, since the cause of divorce has ceased.

Among the wisdoms is that during the period of waiting, the innocence of her womb from her husband becomes known.

{2} And His saying: {So when they have reached their term}; that is, [when] they are near the end of the 'iddah, because if they had completely exited the 'iddah, the husband would not be given the choice between retaining and separating. {Then retain them in good manner}; that is, in a manner of good companionship and fine association, not in a manner of harm, intent on evil, or confinement, for retaining her in that manner is not permissible. {Or part from them in good manner}; that is, a separation without any blame, without mutual abuse or quarrelling, and without compelling her to give up any of her property. {And bring to witness}: over her divorce and her return, {two just men from among you}; that is, two Muslim men of integrity, because in the mentioned witnessing there is a closing of the door to dispute and to concealing what must be made clear by either of them. {And establish the testimony for Allah}; that is, O witnesses, give it in its proper form without addition or deficiency, and intend by its establishment the Face of Allah, the Exalted, and do not show favour to a relative for his kinship or to a friend for his affection. {That}: what we have mentioned to you of rulings and limits {is admonition for whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day}. Indeed, belief in Allah and the Last Day obliges its possessor to be admonished by the admonitions of Allah and to send ahead for his Hereafter the righteous deeds he is able to do, unlike one in whose heart faith has departed, for he does not care what evil he undertakes, nor does he esteem the admonitions of Allah, due to the absence of what would require that. Since divorce may bring about constriction, distress and grief, Allah commanded taqwa (God-consciousness) and promised whoever fears Him in divorce and other matters that He will make for him a way out and an exit. So when a servant wishes to divorce and does so in the lawful manner, by pronouncing a single revocable divorce in a period that is not menstruation and not a purity in which he has had intercourse with her, the matter will not be constricted for him; rather, Allah makes for him a way out and a space by which he is able to return to the marriage if he regrets the divorce.

Although the verse is in the context of divorce and return, the lesson lies in the generality of the wording. Whoever fears Allah [Most High] and holds fast to His pleasure in all his states, Allah will reward him in this world and the Hereafter, and among His rewards is that He makes for him a way out from every hardship and difficulty. Just as whoever fears Allah has a way out made for him, so whoever does not fear Allah falls into burdens and shackles from which he cannot free himself or escape their consequences. Consider this in divorce: when a servant does not fear Allah concerning it, but pronounces it in a forbidden manner, such as three (divorces) or the like, he will inevitably feel a regret he cannot overcome or escape from.

{3} And His saying: {And provide for him from where he does not expect}; that is, Allah brings provision to the God-fearing from a direction he does not anticipate nor perceive. {And whoever relies upon Allah}: in the matter of his religion and his worldly life, by depending upon Allah to bring what benefits him and to ward off what harms him, and trusting Him to facilitate that, {then He is sufficient for him}; that is, He is sufficient for him in the matter in which he relied upon Him. And when the matter is under the guardianship of the Rich, the Strong, the Mighty, the Merciful, then He is nearer to the servant than anything. However, perhaps divine wisdom required delaying it until the time suitable for it; for this reason the Exalted said: {Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose}; that is, the decree and destiny of Allah must take effect without fail. Yet He has made {for everything a measure}; that is, a time and a quantity which it neither exceeds nor falls short of.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 65, verses 6–7:

{6} It has already been established that Allah forbade expelling divorced women from their homes. Here He commands that they be housed, and He specifies that their housing should be according to what is customary (bi-l-ma'ruf), namely a dwelling of the kind that someone of the husband's standing and their standing would live in, in accordance with the husband's means and his hardship. {And do not harm them to make them straitened}; that is: do not harm them while they are housed, by word or by deed, so that they become weary and leave the homes before the end of the waiting period (iddah), with the result that you become the ones who expelled them. The sum of this is that He forbade their expulsion and forbade them from leaving, and commanded that they be housed in a manner that causes them no harm or hardship, and this is referred back to what is customary (al-'urf). {And if they are pregnant}; that is: the divorced women {are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth to their burden}. This is for the sake of the child in the womb if the woman is irrevocably divorced (ba'in), and for her and the child if she is revocably divorced (raj'iyyah). The end of the maintenance is the delivery of the child. When they have delivered their burden, then either they nurse their children or they do not. {Then if they nurse for you, give them their wages}: the wage that was specified for them if one was specified, and otherwise the standard wage for such service (ajr al-mithl). {And consult among yourselves in kindness}; that is: let each of the spouses, and others besides them, command the other with what is good (bi-l-ma'ruf), which is everything that contains benefit and welfare in this world and the next. Neglecting to consult in kindness brings about harm and evil that no one knows but Allah, whereas consultation involves cooperation in righteousness and piety. Fitting to this context is that spouses at the time of separation during the waiting period, especially if a child was born between them, generally fall into disputes and quarrels over the maintenance of the woman and of the child, along with a separation which generally occurs only accompanied by hatred, so that much harm results from it. Therefore each of them is commanded to act with kindness, good companionship, and to avoid enmity and contention, and to give counsel in this. {And if you are in dispute}; that is: if the spouses do not agree upon her nursing the child, {then another woman will nurse for him}: other than her. {And there is no blame upon you if you give what you have agreed upon in kindness}. This applies where the child will accept the breast of someone other than his mother. If he will accept only the breast of his mother, she is designated for his nursing, it becomes obligatory upon her, and she is compelled if she refuses, and she has the standard wage if they have not agreed upon a specified sum. This is derived from the noble verse in meaning: since the child was in his mother's womb for the duration of the pregnancy and had no way out of it, Allah designated for his guardian the obligation of maintenance. When he was born and was able to be sustained by his mother or by someone else, Allah permitted both options. If he is in a state where he cannot be sustained except by his mother, he is in the position of the pregnancy, and his mother is designated as the means of his sustenance.

{7} Then Allah, exalted is He, specified the maintenance according to the husband's condition, saying: {Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth}; that is: let the rich man spend from his riches, so he does not spend the maintenance of the poor. {And whoever has his provision restricted}; that is: constricted for him, {let him spend from what Allah has given him}: from provision. {Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it}. This is consistent with divine wisdom and mercy, for He made each person according to his means, lightened the burden on the one in straitened circumstances, and does not burden him except with what He has given him; Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity, in matters of maintenance and otherwise. {Allah will bring about ease after hardship}: this is good news for those in straitened circumstances that Allah, exalted is He, will remove from them the adversity and lift from them the hardship, for indeed with hardship comes ease; indeed with hardship comes ease.

Therefore each of them is commanded to act with kindness, good companionship, and to avoid enmity and contention, and to give counsel in this. {And if you are in dispute}; that is: if the spouses do not agree upon her nursing the child, {then another woman will nurse for him}: other than her. {And there is no blame upon you if you give what you have agreed upon in kindness}. This applies where the child will accept the breast of someone other than his mother. If he will accept only the breast of his mother, she is designated for his nursing, it becomes obligatory upon her, and she is compelled if she refuses, and she has the standard wage if they have not agreed upon a specified sum. This is derived from the noble verse in meaning: since the child was in his mother's womb for the duration of the pregnancy and had no way out of it, Allah designated for his guardian the obligation of maintenance. When he was born and was able to be sustained by his mother or by someone else, Allah permitted both options. If he is in a state where he cannot be sustained except by his mother, he is in the position of the pregnancy, and his mother is designated as the means of his sustenance.

{7} Then Allah, exalted is He, specified the maintenance according to the husband's condition, saying: {Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth}; that is: let the rich man spend from his riches, so he does not spend the maintenance of the poor. {And whoever has his provision restricted}; that is: constricted for him, {let him spend from what Allah has given him}: from provision. {Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it}. This is consistent with divine wisdom and mercy, for He made each person according to his means, lightened the burden on the one in straitened circumstances, and does not burden him except with what He has given him; Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity, in matters of maintenance and otherwise. {Allah will bring about ease after hardship}: this is good news for those in straitened circumstances that Allah, exalted is He, will remove from them the adversity and lift from them the hardship, for indeed with hardship comes ease; indeed with hardship comes ease.

{8–10} He, exalted is He, informs of His destruction of the rebellious nations and the generations that denied the messengers, and that their numbers and strength did not avail them anything when there came upon them the severe reckoning and the painful punishment. God made them taste of the punishment that was the due consequence of their evil deeds, and along with the punishment of this world, God has prepared for them in the Hereafter a severe punishment. ﴿So fear God, O people of understanding﴾; that is: O you who possess minds that comprehend God's signs and lessons. And [know] that He who destroyed the past generations for their denial, [the same will befall] those after them, who are like them; there is no difference between the two groups.

{11} Then He reminded His worshipers, the believers, of what He sent down to them of His Book, which He revealed to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so as to bring creation out of the darkness of ignorance, disbelief and disobedience into the light of knowledge, faith and obedience. Among people there are those who believed in it and among them are those who did not believe in it. ﴿And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds﴾: [deeds] of obligations and recommended acts, ﴿He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾: therein is enduring bliss such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿Abiding therein forever. God has certainly provided excellent provision for him.﴾ That is: and whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger, those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein forever.

{12} Then He informed that He created the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, and the seven earths and whoever is in them and what is between them, and He sent down the command, which is the legislation and religious rulings that He revealed to His messengers to remind and admonish the servants; and likewise the cosmic and decreed commands by which He manages creation. All of this is so that His servants may know Him and know the all-encompassing power of His capacity over all things and the all-encompassing knowledge of His over all things. When they know Him through His beautiful names and sacred attributes, they worship Him, love Him, and fulfill His right. This is the ultimate purpose of creation and the command: knowledge of God and worship of Him. Those among God's successful righteous servants established this, and the wrongdoers who turn away turned away from it.

The commentary is complete. And praise be to God.
